text: For every finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space E, equipped with its norm-induced metric and Borel sigma algebra, every function V:E→ℝ, and every nonnegative real number κ satisfying κ≥1, suppose V is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable and, for all x,v∈E, κ⁻¹‖v‖² ≤ D²V(x)[v,v] ≤ ‖v‖². Then, for every real number η with 0<η≤1/2, define F:E×E→ℝ by F(y,x)=V(x)+(η⁻¹/2)‖x−y‖². There exists a single Borel-measurable map p:E→E with all of the following properties simultaneously. (1) For every y∈E, p(y)+η∇V(p(y))=y. (2) For every y,z∈E, F(y,p(y))+((κ⁻¹+η⁻¹)/2)‖z−p(y)‖²≤F(y,z), and F(y,z)≤F(y,p(y)) if and only if z=p(y). Thus p(y) is the unique global minimizer of x↦F(y,x), with the stated quantitative lower bound. (3) For every y,y′∈E, ‖p(y)−p(y′)‖≤‖y−y′‖. (4) For every y,y′,G∈E, ‖∇V(p(y)+√η G)−∇V(p(y′)+√η G)‖≤‖y−y′‖. (5) For every y,G,G′∈E, ‖∇V(p(y)+√η G)−∇V(p(y)+√η G′)‖≤√η‖G−G′‖. Here D²V(x)[v,v] is the second Fréchet derivative applied to v twice, ∇V is the gradient with respect to the given real inner product, scalar-vector products are real scalar multiplication, κ⁻¹ is the reciprocal of κ considered as a real number, η⁻¹ is the reciprocal of η, and √η is the nonnegative real square root. The same map p serves every vector input in all five conclusions; it may depend on the ambient structures, V, κ, and η. The constants are exactly those displayed: Hessian bounds κ⁻¹ and 1, quadratic-growth coefficient (κ⁻¹+η⁻¹)/2, Lipschitz bound 1 for p and the common-G gradient comparison, and √η for the comparison in G. All vector inputs, including G and G′, are universally quantified deterministic vectors; no probability law is assumed.
